items.context: agent-manager/api/internal/orchestration/investigation.go:433 explicitly requests `NoLock: true` for investigation runs. Today this also gives investigations the side-effect of accept-all. Once decoupled, investigations would be subject to acceptance rules like any other run. Investigations are documented as read-only analysis flows that build context attachments (event timeline, diffs, history) — they are not expected to write source files. The question is how explicitly we want to prove that and whether to leave any belt-and-braces.

options.label: Leave investigation.go unchanged; add a test that asserts investigation runs do not produce sandbox file changes (so even if acceptance now matters, it is moot).
options.rationale: Recommended. Smallest surface area: NoLock for investigations is correct (they should run concurrently against the same scope without locking out coding runs). The risk is that investigations were silently writing something we missed — a new test pins that they don't, which is the right invariant regardless of this fix.

options.label: Add an explicit acceptance config for investigation runs (e.g., empty allow rules) so they document their write-intent rather than relying on emergent behavior.
options.rationale: More explicit but adds a new construct. Empty allow rules already accept everything (current `evaluateAcceptance` returns Accepted when criteria are empty), so this would not change behavior — it would just document intent in the call site.

options.label: Drop the `NoLock: true` on investigation runs entirely.
options.rationale: Discouraged. NoLock for investigations is load-bearing for concurrency — without it, an investigation against a scope would block coding runs over the same scope. Dropping it changes locking semantics, which is out of this fix's scope.

items.topic: Migration of existing in-flight NoLock=true sandboxes
items.context: Workspace-sandbox persists sandbox records in Postgres (`sandbox_repo.go`). Existing rows with `no_lock = true` were created under the old accept-all assumption. After this fix lands, the next call to `Diff`/`Apply` for those sandboxes will re-evaluate acceptance against the same configured rules. For most sandboxes this is a no-op (no acceptance rules configured → still all accepted). For sandboxes that did configure acceptance rules and rely on the bypass, behavior will change.

options.label: No migration: behavior changes immediately on deploy. Diff/Apply re-evaluates at the next call.
options.rationale: Recommended. The prior behavior was a bug. In practice the only NoLock=true producers in-tree are agent-manager investigation runs (which don't write) and explicit user-driven sandboxes (which would not configure both NoLock=true and meaningful acceptance rules unless they were specifically trying to test the bypass). Sandboxes with no acceptance config still see all-accepted behavior.

options.label: Add a `legacy_accept_all` boolean column on the sandbox table; backfill all current `no_lock=true` rows; preserve their old behavior at evaluateAcceptance; new sandboxes get the new behavior.
options.rationale: Most cautious but adds a permanent schema scar that exists only to grandfather a bug. Hard to ever remove.

options.label: Warn-only mode: log a record at evaluateAcceptance when a NoLock=true sandbox would have been accepted under old semantics but would be rejected under new semantics, for one release; flip to enforced behavior in a follow-up.
options.rationale: Compromise. Adds observability for operators to spot impact. Costs: temporary warn code, two-step rollout, log noise. Worth it only if we suspect significant fleet-wide impact.

items.topic: Test surface and depth of regression coverage
items.context: Spec deliverable #4 calls out 'Regression coverage (assumption tests under scenarios/workspace-sandbox/api/internal/sandbox/**) proving acceptance filtering still applies with NoLock=true, including the multi-sandbox-same-scope case.' No existing tests in service_test.go or assumptions_test.go reference NoLock + acceptance interactions, so this is a greenfield surface. The choice is how deep to go now versus deferring to the e2e item.

options.label: Focused unit tests (4 cases) in service_test.go + 1 back-compat case in assumptions_test.go. No multi-sandbox integration test — defer that to execute/sandbox-runtime-e2e-verification.
options.rationale: Cheapest. Leaves the multi-sandbox-same-scope case to a later layer. Misses the spec's 'multi-sandbox-same-scope' callout at the unit layer.

options.label: Focused unit tests (4 cases in service_test.go + 1 back-compat case in assumptions_test.go) PLUS a service-level integration test that creates two real sandboxes via the Service layer with overlapping scope to verify each evaluates acceptance independently.
options.rationale: Recommended. Honors the spec's explicit multi-sandbox-same-scope callout, while keeping the test surface in this scenario (no agent-manager dependency). Service-layer integration tests already exist in service_test.go, so the harness is in place. The e2e item still owns the spawn-surface verification at a higher layer.

options.label: Full integration coverage: option B plus an end-to-end test that exercises the agent-manager → workspace-sandbox path via the agent-manager investigation flow.
options.rationale: Most thorough but creates a hard cross-scenario test dependency this fix does not need. The spawn-surface verification belongs in execute/sandbox-runtime-e2e-verification.

items.topic: Documentation surface for the 'do not reintroduce' guidance
items.context: AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md already has a one-line note that this fix removes the bypass. The question is whether that's enough, given the original bypass had a comment at the call site that made it look intentional. Future contributors will land at service.go before they land at the docs.

options.label: Inline comment at the (removed) bypass site in evaluateAcceptance referencing AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md Finding 4 M1, plus update AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md to past tense ('was removed') post-merge.
options.rationale: Recommended. Minimal and discoverable from both directions: code reader sees the comment and the contract reference; doc reader sees the historical pointer. Costs almost nothing to maintain.

options.label: Code comment only — AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md already names this fix; an additional doc section would be redundant.
options.rationale: Lighter touch. Risks losing the future-contributor signal in the docs surface.

options.label: Add a 'NoLock and acceptance are orthogonal' entry to scenarios/workspace-sandbox/docs/PROBLEMS.md (under historical pitfalls) plus the code comment plus the contract update.
options.rationale: Most belt-and-braces. PROBLEMS.md is a discoverable failure-mode catalogue; the entry would persist as institutional memory even if AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md changes.

items.text: The helper `noLockFromSandboxConfig` at run_executor.go:1724 returns nil when SandboxConfig.NoLock is false, deliberately letting workspace-sandbox apply its own DefaultNoLock (true). This stays correct after the fix — DefaultNoLock continues to control locking; acceptance is independent.

Greenfield test surface: no existing tests in scenarios/workspace-sandbox/api/internal/sandbox/{service_test.go,assumptions_test.go} reference NoLock or acceptance interactions today. This fix is the first to pin those invariants. Choose Decision 3 with that in mind — the assumption tests added here become the canonical coverage for the orthogonality contract.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold covering: required reading (scientific-debugging, assumption-mapping-and-hardening, test), source-of-truth references with initiative-neighborhood callouts, problem statement, goals, non-goals, scope-aligned acceptance globs, 5-phase approach (code change, config doc, agent-manager investigation handling, regression tests, docs note), test plan with 5 named cases, acceptance criteria, 5-row risk matrix, and explicit cross-initiative implications for the orchestrator. Phases 3, 4, 5 are explicitly gated on round-1 decisions D1, D3, D4.
